hints: Set the limit of the iterative sequence to $x$, giving $x = \sqrt{\dfrac{4}{5 - 2x}}$.
Square both sides, cross-multiply, and rearrange into standard polynomial form to show $2x^3 - 5x^2 + 4 = 0$.
walkthrough:
Assume the iterative sequence converges to a limit $x$. At the limit, $x_{n+1} = x_n = x$:
$$x = \sqrt{\dfrac{4}{5 - 2x}}$$

Square both sides of the equation:
$$x^2 = \dfrac{4}{5 - 2x}$$

Rearrange all terms to one side:
$$2x^3 - 5x^2 + 4 = 0$$
Notice that the left-hand side is exactly $f(x)$. Hence, if the sequence converges, it converges to a root of $f(x) = 0$.

Record each iteration to 4 decimal places until the value justifies $x = 1.28$ to 2 decimal places.
